sections.title: Form and cultivation
sections.text: Lovage is an aromatic perennial native to Iran and Afghanistan, cultivated and naturalised elsewhere. Its flowering stems can reach about 2 m; the foliage clump is often 60–90 cm tall.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The large leaves are divided two or three times. Small yellow-green flowers form umbels and produce aromatic fruits. The leaves, stalks, roots and seeds are used in cooking.

sections.title: Cautions
sections.text: Lovage contains volatile oils and may have a diuretic effect. A university horticultural source describes low-severity toxicity; people with kidney problems or taking medication should seek advice before concentrated use.
